ratings.rationale: Unauthenticated field tampering (W4) is classic T. Support comes only from power-grid and control-system false-data-injection work, so R is analogue-reduced. In-transit alteration of live links needs a strong link adversary. Single-satellite bias is caught at L3 in the strong pass.
ratings.issue: Overlaps T2.03 on 'modified' reports. Cited sources are non-LEO analogues. 'Relay path' is vague: ISL, downlink and backhaul have very different feasibility.

ratings.rationale: Fabricated reports accepted as genuine are spoofing with a ghost-target outcome. Overshadowing was demonstrated on real satellite downlinks, but on EO satellites, not MLAT. A consistent forged set may pass consistency checks. A downlink-segment attacker is organised (T2).
ratings.issue: Same effect and mechanism as T2.09; only the vector wording differs (impersonated node vs overshadowing). Merge, or restrict this one to compromised in-orbit relay nodes.

ratings.rationale: TOA is stamped onboard, so delaying a report does not change its stamped value; it causes latency, staleness or association loss, i.e. flagged degradation. Cited sources support PTP delay and overshadowing, not report delay. Evidence is theoretical and analogue.
ratings.issue: Mechanism flawed: delay or reordering does not distort the time-difference solution unless the CPS uses its own reception time. 'Modified' duplicates T2.01. Sources do not match the claim.

ratings.rationale: Degrading geometric observability is D and by itself yields no wrong report; it only widens the stealth window, so enabler. Link-flooding work (ICARUS, emulators) is simulation on generic LEO networks, not MLAT. HDOP rise is visible at L3.
ratings.issue: Overlaps T2.05 (link denial). Assumes the attacker knows which satellites give best geometry and can select links; selectivity is not shown by the sources.

ratings.rationale: Postulated, no sources. Disrupting crosslinks cuts relay capacity, giving regional degradation. Hard to do against directional ISLs. Link outage is visible in link telemetry at L2.
ratings.issue: No mechanism or vector specified (jamming, cyber, physical). Largely subsumed by T2.04 and by L1 jamming; keep as postulated or merge.

ratings.rationale: Passes the authentication-invariance test: authentic but delayed messages still shift the offset, so tau. PTP and NTP delay attacks were demonstrated on terrestrial systems only. Needs an on-path ISL position. A covert clock bias becomes displacement; L3 catches a single-satellite bias in the strong pass.
ratings.issue: Asset set should include A1.5, the clock that ends up biased. Feasibility of an on-path ISL position is not argued.

ratings.rationale: Authenticating the exchange would stop it, so it fails the invariance test and is S, not tau, with tau as the secondary effect. Forged or replayed PTP is demonstrated on terrestrial NTP/PTP only. Result is clock bias leading to displacement.
ratings.issue: Replay and forgery are distinct sub-threats; replay can survive weak authentication without freshness. Needs an assumed unauthenticated PTP, which should be stated.

ratings.rationale: Passive reception is information disclosure with no direct effect on a report. Eavesdropping on VSAT and Iridium was shown with consumer equipment, but on other networks. Passive capture is undetectable by any system check.
ratings.issue: Tracks and identities derive from public 1090 MHz data, so the disclosure value is overstated. A narrow-beam downlink may not be reachable with consumer gear. Is the downlink encrypted?

ratings.rationale: Overshadowing a downlink is demonstrated on real satellite links (EO, ADS-C context), not LEO MLAT, so analogue. Ghost targets are Deception. Needs placement near a ground station and a tracking antenna, so T2. Consistent fabricated sets may escape L3 checks.
ratings.issue: Canonical record for downlink injection; T2.02 duplicates it. Reports also fall under asset A2.1, and the consistency check against ADS-B for ghost targets is unspecified.

ratings.rationale: Passive capture of commands is disclosure, a precondition for forged telecommands. Support is a general Iridium talk and a design framework, not telecommand capture on an MLAT constellation, so theoretical and analogue. Undetectable.
ratings.issue: Weakly supported: the cited work does not show telecommand capture. Uplink capture needs presence in the beam or at the ground station. Overlaps T2.08 in method.

ratings.rationale: Accepted forged commands give control of the command path (E). On-orbit hacking sandboxes and satellite firmware analyses show feasibility on other platforms. Needs uplink capability and keys or weak authentication. Shared credentials could reach the whole constellation. Multi-satellite effects exceed W2.
ratings.issue: Conditional on T4.04 and T1.12, so it is a compound threat. Impact set depends on command content (clock, firmware, thresholds); the A1.6 asset is missing.

ratings.rationale: Device compromise is a foothold; the consequence comes through T2.01, T2.03 or T2.04, so enabler. SATCOM terminal flaws and the 2022 SATCOM provider incidents are observed, but outside MLAT. A shared gateway touches several footprints. Detected by IT monitoring, not by L3 checks.
ratings.issue: Overlaps A3.7 platform compromise at L3 and the downstream tampering threats. Asset should include network devices not in the register. Sources are generic SATCOM.

missing_threats.title: Replay of genuine reports
missing_threats.why: Replaying authentic old reports yields ghost associations and wrong geometry without forgery; distinct from T2.01 and T2.02.

missing_threats.title: Ground-station uplink/downlink jamming
missing_threats.why: Jamming a ground station is a single point of regional denial and is not covered.

missing_threats.title: PTP denial forcing clock holdover
missing_threats.why: Suppressing PTP exchanges leaves clocks free-running, producing drift without any forged or delayed message.

missing_threats.title: ISL routing or control-plane manipulation
missing_threats.why: Route poisoning or scheduling manipulation can redirect, delay or drop reports with no physical link disruption.

missing_threats.title: Downlink or ground-station modem compromise
missing_threats.why: Modem and baseband firmware at the ground station sits on the TB2 path and is not represented.

rubric_ambiguities: Enabler versus disclosure-only: both have no direct consequence, yet Damage 1 exists for disclosure and null for enablers.
Affected users for link-level root events is unclear: one link, one footprint, or the aircraft downstream.
Di_strong and Di_weak are defined for bias; they do not clearly apply to fabricated targets, passive interception or denial.
Tier ranges such as T2-T3 for AC4 and AC5 force a choice without a stated tie-break.
Mixed evidence, e.g. a mix of E2 analogues and no direct support, has no rule for choosing the level.
batch_comments.overall: A reasonably coherent L2 batch, but T2.02 and T2.09 are near-duplicates, T2.03's mechanism is technically doubtful (TOA is stamped onboard), and T2.01 rests only on analogue evidence. The PTP pair is well scoped and the invariance test separates them cleanly. Several threats are conditional on others, and a few vectors lack feasibility arguments.
